title: failure-recovery-usability
rawUserRequest: WI-21 failure-recovery-usability: ensure ordinary users can recover from interruption, upgrade failure, locks, branch recovery failure, conflicts, incomplete closure, stale evidence, unknown sources, and unavailable providers without reading source code.

rawRequestSource.reference: AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation instructions, WI-21; active user goal

declaredIntent.summary: Make recovery status, writes, rollback, remaining state, next command, and human intervention machine-readable and human-usable.

outOfScope: Provider configuration and external provider recovery operations.

sources.reason: Closure recovery and state evidence baseline.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: interruption, upgrade failure, lock, branch, and conflict recovery have complete user guidance
closure, stale evidence, unknown source, and unavailable provider report safe next steps

riskAssessment.reason: Ambiguous recovery guidance can cause unsafe repeated operations.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: Recovery reports and deterministic fixtures can be implemented and tested locally.

preReviewWarnings: Do not claim that local recovery tests prove provider recovery.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Recovery guidance records current state, writes, rollback, remaining state, next command, and human-intervention need for every declared failure mode.
Recovery validation rejects incomplete recovery guidance and unknown failure modes.
Tests cover interruption, upgrade failure, lock, branch, conflict, closure, stale evidence, unknown source, and provider-unavailable scenarios.
Documentation explains the human-readable recovery boundary.
guidelines: Recovery guidance must state what was and was not rolled back before offering a next command.
Fail closed when a recovery scenario lacks state, write, rollback, next-command, or human-intervention information.
Do not modify provider configuration or claim provider recovery evidence.

intent.problem: Existing recovery details can require source-code interpretation instead of giving a normal user an actionable state-aware path.
constraints: Do not claim local fixtures prove provider recovery.
intent.rationale: A small structured recovery report makes failure state and the safe next command explicit without hiding unrecovered state.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Set only when a human explicitly approves restricted governance paths.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
